newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta harvest near 75 percent complete.
newsitem.headline: Alberta harvest near 75 percent complete.

text.p: Alberta's crop harvest was just under 75 percent complete Tuesday, bolstered by warm weather and drying winds, Alberta Agriculture said in a crop update.
"As a province, just under three quarters of the crop has been harvested," it said.
The south completed harvest and the extreme north end of the Peace River Valley was almost done. Northeast Alberta was the furthest behind at 30 to 40 percent finished.
Almost all cereals in swath in the past two to three weeks were expected to grade as Number Three or feed grade quality.
Oilseeds seemed to have fared much better than cereals.
Southern Alberta wrapped up its harvest except for sugar beets and potatoes.

Central Alberta was 50 percent harvested in the west but quality was questionable. The eastern half harvested 65 percent of crops. Scattered showers prevented any significant progress from being made.
Northeast Alberta reported the harvest there was 70 percent complete in the south, and in the north, 35 percent. Smoky Lake, Wainwright, Lamont and St. Paul districts were 50 percent complete.
Crops left standing over the past two to three weeks should see better grades than those swathed.
Northwest Alberta had harvested 30 to 35 percent of its crop.

The Peace River Valley's northern Fort Vermillion and Manning districts were 95 percent harvested but the rest of the region was 30 percent complete. Quality was less than ideal with some producers expecting Number Three and feed grades in wheat.
